title: Exec takeaway one-pager + Renewal signal plan
body:
Purpose: A compact, boardroom-ready executive takeaway (one page) and a short renewal-signal plan that CSMs can use to brief executive sponsors and trigger renewal motions. This is intentionally concise so it can be pasted into slide notes, sent as an email, or used as the front of a QBR packet.

1) Executive one-pager (single-screen / slide) — layout and copy
- Header: Customer, Quarter, CSM, Exec Sponsor(s), Renewal Date, Contract ARR
- Topline headline (1 sentence): e.g., "Reliable inference at scale: 95% SLA attainment and 2.4x embedding throughput since last quarter"
- KPIs (3–5 bullets, 1 metric each):
  - Uptime / SLO: 99.97% (target 99.9%)
  - Avg latency (p50/p95): 110ms / 280ms (improved 18% p95 vs last quarter)
  - Cost per 1M tokens: $220 (vs $265 target; -17%)
  - Product value metric (customer-specific): e.g., search relevance lift +12% on top queries
  - Tickets / SEV incidents: 1 (SEV3) in quarter, resolved in 9 hours
- Progress vs commitments (3 bullets): short statement per commitment, status (green/amber/red) and owner
- Roadmap alignment (1 sentence): e.g., "Upcoming release: per-route caching (ETA Q3) reduces burst cost for PPAs"
- Renewal health signal (single line with rationale): GREEN | YELLOW | RED + 1-sentence explanation
- Ask / next steps (3 bullets): executive-level asks (e.g., approval for dedicated burst capacity, quarterly technical review cadence, exec sponsor intro to procurement)

2) Renewal signal checklist (what to look for — quick triggers)
- Green signals: steady usage growth, SLA met, low escalation volume, CSAT >= 4.2
- Yellow signals: usage plateauing, 1–2 missed non-critical SLO targets, procurement delay >30 days, feature parity concerns
- Red signals: repeated high-severity incidents, sudden spike in latency/failed requests, legal/compliance blockers, churn intent from product owner
- Immediate actions per color:
  - Green: schedule renewal talk 90 days out, offer early-bird discounts for multi-quarter commit
  - Yellow: prioritize technical deep-dive + run a short remediation POC (2 weeks)
  - Red: escalate to AM and Solutions Eng, propose dedicated capacity or rollback plan, prepare renewal contingency brief

3) Suggested 15-minute executive sponsor update agenda (phone / 1:1)
- 0:00–0:02: Quick greeting + confirm timebox
- 0:02–0:05: One-line topline (metrics & health color)
- 0:05–0:09: Product impact stories (1 customer anecdote or one key metric trend)
- 0:09–0:11: Risks & mitigations (1–2 bullets)
- 0:11–0:14: Renewal signal and ask (what we need from sponsor: decision, intro to procurement, budget alignment)
- 0:14–0:15: Next steps and scheduling (QBR, technical workshop, procurement touchpoint)

4) Customer-facing quarterly recap email template (short, executive-friendly)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Q[Quarter] Recap and next steps
Hi <Exec Name>,

Quick recap from our Q[Quarter] partnership review: overall health is [GREEN/YELLOW/RED]. Highlights: uptime 99.97%, average latency improved 18% vs prior quarter, and production embedding throughput is up 2.4x. We resolved the single SEV3 incident in 9 hours; engineering recommendations are implemented.

Planned next steps: 1) Technical workshop to walkthrough per-route caching (proposed week of <date>), 2) Confirm renewal timeline and procurement contacts (target: <renewal date minus 60 days>), 3) Explore a 3-month burst reservation to stabilize cost during expected peak.

Would you be available for a 15-minute check-in next week to confirm the procurement owners and timeline?

Thanks,
<CSM name>

5) Customer-facing quarterly recap email template (detailed with attachments)
Subject: Q[Quarter] Customer Recap, health summary, and renewal cadence
Hi <Stakeholder Group>,

Attached: one-pager PDF (topline metrics), incident timeline, usage & cost dashboard link.
Summary bullets:
- Business impact: Topline product metric improved +12% (search relevance example)
- Reliability: 99.97% uptime, p95 latency down 18%
- Cost: cost/unit improved 17% vs plan; detailed forecast attached
- Support: 1 SEV3 (root cause: infra burst throttle); mitigation: autoscale config change and KV cache deployed

Recommended cadence: Exec sponsor touchpoint monthly, Product-led walkthrough quarterly, Procurement sync 60/30/7 days before renewal.

Please confirm who should join the procurement sync and whether the legal team needs blinded SOW language.

Regards,
<CSM name> + Solutions Eng

6) Renewal mini-tracker (copyable into sheet)
- Renewal date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Current ARR: $<amount>
- Contract type: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- Health color: GREEN/YELLOW/RED
- Procurement owner + email: <name> / <email>
- Last exec touchpoint: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Next planned action: <e.g., schedule procurement sync>

7) Risk scripts / handling brief (what to say if sponsor raises concerns)
- If cost is called out: "We recommend a short audit and a 2-week POC on targeted quantization + batching; team can show forecasted unit cost improvement before renewal."
- If reliability is raised: "We’ll propose a remediation plan with a 30-day SLO remediation target and a fallback policy (regional failover) during the window."
- If procurement stalls: "Would an intro to procurement and a pre-approved SOW template speed this? We can supply procurement-friendly data sheets and a 30-day trial extension."

8) Attachments + assets to include with the one-pager/email
- One-pager PDF (export of the page above)
- Dashboard link: usage / cost / incidents (add link)
- Incident postmortem (if relevant)
- Proposed SOW language / sample renewal discount options

9) CSM checklist before sending to exec sponsor
- [ ] One-pager populated and approved by Solutions Eng
- [ ] Dashboard links verified and timeboxed
- [ ] Procurement and legal contact identified
- [ ] Renewal mini-tracker updated in CRM (CSM must set next touch date)
- [ ] Exec sponsor ask simplified into 1–2 bullets

Appendix: sample quick copy for slide notes (paste into a slide):
"Topline: We’re in a [GREEN/YELLOW/RED] health state. The platform delivered 2.4x throughput and reduced p95 latency by 18% this quarter. Only one SEV3 occurred and it was resolved inside our SLA window; mitigations are deployed. Recommended next step is a 15-minute sponsor touch to confirm procurement cadence and explore a short reserved burst for the upcoming traffic window."

Notes on usage: keep the one-pager to one printed page. For exec audiences prefer bullets and a single visual metric (trend sparkline). If the renewal is >90 days out, move to low-touch cadence (quarterly). If <=60 days, switch to a weekly renewal tracker and escalate any yellow signals to AM/AE.

End of doc.
